A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original visual-versus-textual question-answering results, activation-patching experiments and attention-knockout results, including qualitative appendix examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original POPVQA evaluations across five models, revised activation-patching experiments, statistical analyses and appendix results.

M1.justification: The central forward-patching intervention changes substantively. v1 Section 3.2 replaces image hidden states only at layer 19; v2 Section 6 and Figure 2 freeze source-layer states across intervening layers. This changes both visual-state processing and the representations available to query tokens during the intervention. Cross-entity patching and attention knockout are retained.

E1.justification: The IMDB-WIKI celebrity-image evaluation is replaced by POPVQA, covering celebrities, landmarks, paintings and brand logos using Wikidata images. v2 also evaluates cross-type entity patching. These changes broaden represented populations and intervention scenarios beyond simply increasing sample size.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates only LLaVA-1.5-7B. v2 Table 1 adds LLaVA-MORE-8B with CLIP and SigLIP, LLaVA-1.6-34B and Qwen2-VL. Figures 4–5 also compare the two LLaVA-MORE variants with LLaVA7B in the intervention experiments; these are evaluated comparators, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: v1 uses 300 recognized entities sampled from 10,000 images; v2 selects model-specific recognized subsets from 15,395 POPVQA pairs, including 925 for LLaVA7B. The early-identification analysis changes models and its cutoff from layers below 10 to below 5. Cross-type patching adds category-neutral prompts. The revised patching endpoint is inconsistently documented as layer 20 in Section 6 and layer 19 in Figure 5's caption.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-type patching to test whether late visual information overrides an earlier entity category, expands backbone comparisons, and reworks early/late identification analysis to include textual accuracy as a control. Appendix A adds entity-type analyses. The attention-knockout curve and LeBron James/Donald Trump examples are retained from v1, not newly added analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds Wilcoxon signed-rank tests comparing paired per-entity visual and textual accuracies, with overall and entity-type p-values in Table 4. This adds a statistical check to the accuracy comparison. Shaded intervention curves already appear in v1; neither version discloses repeated-run or seed counts.

E6.justification: v1 reports LLaVA accuracies of 38% visual and 52% textual; v2 Table 1 reports 27.6% and 45.3% on its different recognized cohort. These are replaced results, not same-setting performance changes. v2 adds extensive model, patching and subgroup results, including Qwen2-VL's reversed gap for paintings: 44.5% visual versus 27.6% textual in Table 3.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems, proofs or formal theoretical assumptions. The expanded VLM notation is mathematically equivalent to the earlier setup. Revised patching assignments specify an experimental intervention change rather than new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: v2 makes POPVQA construction and release an explicit central contribution alongside mechanistic analysis, and extends its conclusions across models and visual backbones. The abstract changes an average 19% accuracy-drop claim to a drop reaching 18% for some models. The central hypothesis of late visual-information integration remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving backbone alignment, model depth and training, and interprets the early-identification results using corresponding textual accuracy to argue that stronger entity knowledge underlies early recognition. It adds stale-fact and entity-type qualifications. Limitations now distinguish broad benchmarking from mechanistic probing restricted to LLaVA-style models, replacing the earlier single-model restriction.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands dataset documentation: popularity-based selection, aspect-preserving padding and resizing to 336 by 336, question filtering, multiple acceptable answers and dataset regeneration instructions. It adds a separate POPVQA access link and licensing/IRB disclosures. The existing code-repository link and A100/H100 hardware disclosure are retained; these are not new resource disclosures.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around PopQA, InfoSeek and ViQuAE, modality-contribution studies, cross-modal knowledge conflicts and human picture superiority. These additions explain how its dataset and two-step analysis differ from prior approaches. Publication updates for retained works such as Neo et al. do not themselves constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the narrative around a dedicated Problem Setup, dataset section, motivating experiment and two standalone intervention sections. It moves and expands notation, rewrites the experimental roadmap and intervention explanations, and standardizes terminology such as visual/textual representations. This is substantive restructuring beyond section renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds an intervention schematic and dataset overview, redesigns the single-model intervention plots as multi-panel and grouped-bar comparisons, and adds four quantitative tables. The original motivating illustration is retained; the attention-knockout figure and qualitative table become Figure 6 and Table 5 through relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow evidence base of one model and 300 celebrity images. The broader benchmark tests generality across entity types and models, while paired significance tests and the textual control strengthen assessment of the gap and early-identification findings. Dataset documentation also improves reproducibility. These gains outweigh identifiable reporting defects: Section 4 reverses the CLIP/SigLIP recognition comparison despite Table 1 showing 844 versus 660 entities, and Section 6 conflicts with Figure 5 over the patching endpoint.
